    External MCP Server Catalog¶

    Beyond CorpusIQ's 40+ built-in connectors, the MCP ecosystem now has 22,000+ servers spanning every domain. This catalog tracks the most relevant third-party MCP servers for business operators - curated from mcp.so and mcpservers.org.

    Last updated: November 24, 2026 (evening sweep) · The three newest sweep reports are below. The condensed pass-by-pass history, back to the first pass, is in the catalog sweep log.

    🆕 November 24, 2026 - Evening Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)¶

    Fired on the 21:00 MST tick, ten hours after the 18:00Z supplement stored its baseline, and the directory did not move: the twelve numbered server maps returned 37,599 raw <loc> entries against 37,599 with every per-map count identical (4,129 / 2,527 / 2,945 / 3,200 / 3,290 / 2,891 / 5,878 / 2,739 / 2,606 / 2,575 / 2,509 / 2,310), the distinct key set 23,892 on both bases under one normalizer, and not one of 34,152 lastmod rows at or after the cutoff, the newest stamp 17:53:49Z in both captures. The like-for-like set diff is 0 additions and 0 removals; the stored baseline file reads 23,906 only because the earlier extractor kept fourteen locale prefixes as keys (de/servers through zh-TW/servers). All three ships came from the two surfaces that do not depend on the sitemaps: the feed answered 200 at 160,044 bytes with 44 anchors, 30 stamps and four cards above the cutoff, and the queue carried #8005 to #8035, thirty-one filings. Two of the three ships are keyless or discovery-open, and the third lands on a complete OAuth chain.

    • WeightedShares MCP - Buybacks, SBC and True FCF - the catalogue's first buyback-versus-stock-compensation surface, and the first entry with a filed-dollar control: keyless initialize 200 at https://weightedshares.com/mcp as weightedshares-sec-mcp 1.0.0, five tools and all five driven. Apple's five-year window reads cashBuybacksUsd 439,002,000,000 against sbcExpenseUsd 58,211,000,000, turning standard FCF of 554,657,000,000 into True FCF of 496,446,000,000 at a 24.06% margin while the diluted count still falls 12.72%; the FY2026 buyback of 86,390,000,000 matches SEC companyconcept PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock for CIK 0000320193 to the dollar. The screen is the argument: GM retired -32.52% of its shares in five years with stock compensation at 6.80% of buyback dollars against MSFT at 46.26%. Two gaps recorded: foreign issuers return nulls with a 20-F ADS notice instead of zeros, and a non-flagship window can end two fiscal years back (TSM reads FY2019-FY2024). Free, CC BY 4.0 with attribution.
    • Transept MCP - Document Translation With Review Gates - a translation workspace rather than a translate endpoint: keyless initialize 200 and a keyless tools/list returning 42 tools at https://app.transept.ai/api/public/v1/mcp (transept 1.0.0, registry ai.transept/transept 1.0.0 and 1.0.1). The design is in the server's own instructions: documents split into blocks, run_estimate free before run_start needs confirm: true, estimates that are ceilings with the unused reserve released, review gates answering gate_pending with a finding_count, and strings_reimport returning delta_block_ids so only changed units are re-translated. Execution is gated by a JSON-RPC error -32001 that names the fix ("mint one under Settings -> Developer") with no content block and no isError field, a refusal shape that renders as nothing in most clients. MCP starts at Lite, EUR 9 / USD 10 for 25,000 credits; one credit per source word, three in Pro mode, 68 languages.
    • ReleasePad MCP - Publish Your Changelog From Chat - the catalogue's first changelog surface, shipped on a full OAuth chain: initialize refused 401 with WWW-Authenticate naming resource_metadata, the protected-resource document answering 200 with scopes read and write, and an RFC 8414 document with dynamic registration, PKCE S256, refresh grants and none client auth on the same host as the MCP endpoint. Two constraints worth an afternoon each: the only response mode is query and /.well-known/openid-configuration is a 404 HTML page, so there is no OIDC layer. The catalogue value is the entitlement and the default: MCP access requires Pro at USD 35 a month per product, the free plan carries 20 posts and no MCP, every post starts as a draft, the grant is read-only or full access, destructive tools are flagged for client confirmation, and revocation is per-app in Connected Apps. Tool names are unreadable without an account and the guide records capabilities rather than pretending to a schema.

    Also identified this pass (not catalogued). AgentsRank (feed, 23:58Z) is the strongest hold and the reason is audience, not quality: keyless initialize 200 and 33 tools for an agent hub of worker search, job posting, reputation and messaging, registry ai.agentsrank/agentsrank 2.1.0 to 2.4.0, held on the agent-tooling lane this catalogue already carries. Sports DataFeeds by Rolling Insights (21:29Z) answers 401 with no WWW-Authenticate on a class Vublox Sports and the keyless odds surface already own. Energieausweis Express (20:21Z) is held on EcoExperten Energieausweis.     🆕 November 24, 2026 - Midday Supplement (4 New, 4 Guides)¶

    Fired on the 11:00 MST tick, one hour after the midday pass closed at 17:00Z. The directory was flat: 57 fewer raw <loc> entries, twelve more keys, 18 restamped rows and one new feed card. The material came from the midday pass's own hold list. It read six feed products in one line each and catalogued none; this pass drove four of them to their gates and catalogued all four. Three of these four guides therefore reverse a hold taken an hour earlier, and the reversal is recorded rather than hidden.

    • Codixio MCP - E-Invoices, Tariff Codes, Localization - the window's one card at 17:12Z, and the only genuine arrival. Keyless initialize refuses 401 on /mcp and on all three per-service routes with no WWW-Authenticate; the documented path is OAuth 2.1 with the client registering itself. Three EU compliance jobs priced per call from prepaid credit: an e-invoice checked against the official KoSIT validator at 0.10 EUR, a CN/TARIC suggestion at 1.50 EUR, a marketplace listing rewritten to the target country's rules at 9.90 EUR, 10.00 EUR minimum top-up through Polar, no subscription. Six tools across four endpoints, so the boundary is an address chosen at connect time, and the ceiling is published: tariff confidence is high only for German descriptions.
    • ZeroBounce MCP - Email Validation Inside the Assistant - held an hour ago on "the MailTester email-verification trio", which was the right class and the wrong verdict. This is the vendor's own server, not a wrapper, and the same tools ship as @zerobounce/mcp on npm under MIT for clients that cannot open a browser. Every tool carries readOnlyHint/destructiveHint and states whether it spends credits or changes the account, and the README names the two endpoints the vendor deliberately does not expose: the Inbox Placement webhook and the Warmup SMTP password test. $39 for 2,000 addresses to start, ONE at $99 a month with 10,000 credits, one credit per validation, 20 per successful Email Finder query.
    • Persado MCP - Score Marketing Copy Before You Send - held on "marketing copy generation", which undersells it: it does not generate, it scores 0 to 100 with the elements moving the score named, then ranks rewrites by predicted lift. The most complete chain of the four: 401 with resource_metadata, one permission scope (mcp:tools), and an RFC 8414 document from a Keycloak realm with PKCE S256, refresh grants, a registration endpoint and none client auth, where the issuer is not the host a client connects to. 14-day trial, no card; brand voice and the 20+ regulatory frameworks are labelled Enterprise.
    • Figment MCP - A Mac Rented by the Hour, Ordered by an Agent - held on two words, "mac hosting", for the least classifiable entry of the day. The only keyless 200 of the window: figment-mac 1.0.0, eight tools, and figment_get_offer driven live to offer_version mac-offer-2026-11-17 with $0.15/hour Intel VM, $0.40/hour shared M4 Pro and $1.00/hour dedicated M4 Pro. The catalogue value is the money loop, not the hardware: a keyless create_account hands back an api_key once, buy_credit returns a Stripe Checkout link a person pays, the first purchase is $25, billing runs by the minute and stops only on the stop call because "a guest shutdown alone does not stop charges", and the structural ceiling is two running Macs per account.

    Fired on the 03:00 MST tick, 5.7 hours after the evening pass stored its baseline at 04:24Z. The directory added nothing: the twelve numbered server maps returned the same 37,769 raw <loc> entries with a block that sums exactly (4,171 / 2,516 / 2,936 / 3,221 / 3,327 / 2,906 / 5,864 / 2,739 / 2,634 / 2,575 / 2,524 / 2,356), the distinct key set 23,894 on both captures, and 34,486 lastmod rows with not one at or after the 04:30Z cutoff, the newest stamp anywhere being 00:27:03Z. The material came from the two surfaces that do not depend on the sitemaps: the feed answered 200 at 159,377 bytes with 30 cards, 30 stamps and five above the cutoff, and its anchors are back after last evening's React-shell regression, so the slug-to-stamp pairing recipe works again. The queue carried #7941 to #7965, twenty-five filings in five hours. Both ships are operator products behind a complete OAuth chain, which is the tier this catalogue trusts when no credential exists.

    • Spacestack MCP - Venue Bookings Inside the Assistant - a mcpservers.org arrival and a feed card at 04:10Z, and the catalog's first venue-management entry. The chain measures end to end: 401 with resource_metadata, a protected-resource document naming exactly two scopes (spacestack:read, spacestack:write) and the MCP host as its own authorization server, and an RFC 8414 document with authorization code, refresh, dynamic registration and PKCE S256. The permission model is the reason to read it: the connector acts as the signed-in team member with that person's role, the connect step offers Read only or Read and write per person, a workspace switch is off by default and turning it off disconnects everyone straight away, and the assistant cannot delete, message a client, take or refund a payment, or touch billing. What it does is the venue's day: is this date free, what tours are this week, add the lead, book the tour, and it asks before emailing the guest a confirmation. $99 per venue a month billed yearly, $1,188 a venue a year, unlimited seats, 30-day trial with no card.
    • Vidocu MCP - Documents Turned Into Training Videos - a feed card at 08:11Z and the opposite of an identity token: 17 resource scopes on the protected-resource document, 44 on the authorization server, from videos:write to locks:write, with PKCE S256 and a two-host split where the issuer is api.vidocu.ai and the sign-in screen is vidocu.ai. Its work is operator work: a PDF, DOCX, PPTX or Keynote becomes one finished video unattended, a video becomes a step-by-step help article, get_article reads one back without paying to regenerate it, and get_credit_costs prices a job first. 146 tools by the vendor's documentation against 168 on the listing, a 22-tool gap recorded rather than reconciled. Analysis is 50 credits a minute, so a 10-minute walkthrough is a Starter plan's whole month, and the Knowledge Center add-on is $100 a month on paid plans.

    Data Firewall Suite (PortEden)¶

    The PortEden Secure* family puts a data firewall between AI agents and your Google/Microsoft accounts. Every action is permission-gated, content-redacted, and audit-logged. One-click revoke. Complementary to CorpusIQ's read-only external-source retrieval model.

    Secure Calendar (Google Calendar & Outlook)¶

    Search schedule, check availability, create/reschedule/cancel events, RSVP. AI held to permissions you grant. Every change logged.

    Secure Email (Gmail & Outlook)¶

    Search, read, send, reply, forward, label, delete email. Sensitive content redacted before AI sees it. Full audit trail.

    Secure Google Drive¶

    Search, read, create, copy, rename, move, share, delete files and folders. Sensitive data redacted. Permission-gated.

    Secure Google Docs¶

    Search, read, create, copy, rename, precisely edit documents (insert, append, replace). Every edit logged.

    Secure Google Sheets¶

    Create/copy spreadsheets, read tabs/ranges, write/append values, manage tabs. Protects sensitive values, audits every write.

    Secure Google Sheets MCP Server ★ New¶

    Dedicated MCP server for PortEden's Google Sheets data firewall. Read, write, and manage spreadsheet data with permission gating and audit logging. Separate from the Drive-level Secure Google Drive server.

    Memory & Knowledge¶

    Exomem ★ New (Aug 17)¶

    Local-first memory substrate for MCP agents - hybrid FTS5 + vector search over your own Markdown/Obsidian vault, governed review queues, evidence and supersession in plain files; measured 864 ms hybrid find at 50,000 notes. AGPL-3.0, pip install exomem, no account. (open source) · Guide →

    Persistent Memory for Coding Assistants MCP ★ New (July 14)¶

    Persistent memory and cross-session learning for AI coding assistants. Cloud-based context management via MCP. Redundant category (3+ memory MCPs already catalogued). INDEX ONLY.

    Cortex Memory MCP ★ New (July 4)¶

    Structured memory layer for AI agents - persistent knowledge storage with retrieval and context management. Provides AI agents with long-term memory capabilities across sessions. Essential for operators building stateful AI agent workflows that require memory persistence.

    Psychopathia Machinalis MCP ★ New (July 4)¶

    Read-only MCP tools over the Psychopathia Machinalis nosology - 79 conditions across the AI-psychopathology taxonomy, via 11 tools. Zero-install hosted endpoint available. Niche but notable for AI safety researchers and operators running agent evaluation/red-teaming pipelines.

    Astucia Wiki MCP ★ New (July 4)¶

    AI-enabled team wiki with semantic search, auto-organization, and MCP-native read/write access. Built from the ground up for AI agent consumption - finally, a wiki your agents can actually query and update. Integration Guide · astucia.wiki

    Anki MCP ★ Official¶

    Enable AI assistants to interact with Anki spaced-repetition flashcards.

    XMemo¶

    Persistent memory for AI agents across sessions.

    Vault Cortex ★ New¶

    MCP server for Obsidian vaults - search, memory, link graph, 23 tools, OAuth-protected. Connect AI agents to your Obsidian knowledge base. Ideal for operators who use Obsidian as their second brain.

    Frinus ★ New¶

    MCP server exposing 70 tools spanning cognitive memory, working memory, sessions, agents, the L0-L3 knowledge hierarchy, orchestration tasks, and training pipelines. Speaks stdio, consumed by Claude Desktop, Claude Code, OpenCodex, and any MCP-aware client. Enterprise-grade AI memory infrastructure for operators building knowledge-intensive agent systems.

    Agent Magnet ★ New¶

    Self-learning memory for AI tools - remembers user preferences and context across Claude, Cursor, and Codex with multi-parameter forgetting and cross-tool identity. Keeps your AI agents consistent across sessions and platforms. Ideal for operators who work across multiple MCP clients and want persistent, self-improving agent context.

    Linksee Memory MCP ★ New¶

    Memory with drift detection for AI agents - detects context staleness and signals when agent memory needs refresh. For operators running multi-session agent workflows where context accuracy is critical. npx -y linksee-memory

    Memclaw ★ New ★ Featured¶

    Governed, shared, self-improving memory for AI agent fleets - built for multi-tenant, multi-agent production environments. Apache 2.0. 131 GitHub stars. Production-proven: eToro runs 300+ agents on Memclaw (26,500+ memories, 1,372 shared skills, 23ms p50 search). Features: tenant isolation, visibility scopes (agent/team/org), agent trust tiers (0-3), full audit trails, single-pass LLM enrichment (14 memory types), hybrid search (pgvector + full-text + knowledge graph), contradiction detection, and PII auto-flagging. Managed platform at memclaw.net or self-hosted via Docker. pip install memclaw-client or npm install @caura/memclaw-client. Essential for operators running fleets of AI agents who need governed, shared memory with production-grade isolation and audit.

    Memory Engine ★ New (June 29)¶

    Atomic memory model for AI agents - knowledge stored as atoms (facts, decisions, events, preferences, logs, procedures, notes, session messages). Multi-factor ranking combines FTS relevance × confidence × recency × weight (not just BM25). Organic decay and reinforcement over time. Essential for operators building AI agents that need sophisticated, long-term memory with context-aware recall beyond simple vector search. github.com/SimoneB79/memory-engine

    memo ★ New (July 1)¶

    100% local persistent semantic memory for AI agents on Apple Silicon (MLX) or Linux/Ubuntu (CPU). Markdown source of truth, sqlite-vec + BM25 hybrid search, codegraph-backed knowledge graph. MCP server + CLI. No cloud, no API keys. Privacy-first memory infrastructure for operators who need local-only AI agent memory without cloud dependencies. Essential for regulated industries (HIPAA, GDPR) or operators who refuse cloud-based memory infrastructure. github.com/jagoff/memo · pip install mlx-memo

    SPM - Structured Project Memory ★ New (July 2)¶

    Project-scoped memory for AI agents with provenance tracking and access control. Delivered as a remote MCP connector - context packs, verification, context graphs, and cryptographic memory integrity. Essential for operators running multi-agent workflows who need auditable, verifiable project memory with governance. github.com/getspm/spm-agent-connectors · Integration Guide

    How to Use External MCP Servers¶

    Most MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Hermes) support multiple MCP server connections simultaneously. To add an external server alongside CorpusIQ:

    {
 "mcpServers": {
 "corpusiq": {
 "url": "https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp",
 "transport": "streamable-http"
 },
 "firecrawl": {
 "command": "npx",
 "args": ["-y", "firecrawl-mcp"],
 "env": {
 "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY": "fc-YOUR_KEY"
 }
 },
 "playwright": {
 "command": "npx",
 "args": ["@playwright/mcp@latest"]
 }
 }
}

    Check each server's documentation for specific transport type (streamable HTTP, stdio, SSE) and authentication requirements.
